title: Guard watch
summary: A finder over the credential deny-list: every pointer resolves, none sits inside the kit or a limb-readable root, and no secret-shaped file has been written into the tree.

surfaces.usb: DEGRADED(promotion pending - authored and certified on PC first, then carried to the stick per-file and hash-verified, where the stick runs its own suite)
surfaces.web: N/A(by steward decision 2026-09-20: a browser tab has no local tree, no credential pointers and no roots to audit, so a card there could only be decoration)

notes: Finder (family 'watch') over the credential deny-list. THE HARD RULE: it never opens a credential file and never prints a secret - it stats, resolves and compares paths only, and where a git remote URL carries a token it reports that fact WITHOUT printing the URL, because the URL is the secret. Its direct consequence is stated in missing[] every time: a secret inside a file whose name looks ordinary is beyond this card, because finding it would mean reading it. IT ASKS, IT DOES NOT RE-DERIVE: the deny rule is tools._denied(resolved_path) - the kernel's own, which resolves a path to its real form first so a short name, junction or mapped letter cannot slip past it - and the pointers/roots/drives come from admin_map. Keeping a second copy of the deny list would be a module that duplicates kernel logic, which is already wrong. GREEN MEANS EVERY CHECK RAN AND FOUND NOTHING: a check that could not run is named in checks.unchecked and drags the card to amber, never green. A pointer that does not resolve on a drive that is not present is 'lives elsewhere' and NOT a fault (the stick does not carry the steward's I: ops keys); on a drive that IS present it is a finding. The wide scan is bounded to depth 3 inside a shared 4,000-entry budget and says so; the kit walk has no depth limit because the kit is small enough to walk whole. It owns no state, writes nothing, fixes nothing - its own test scans this file for write calls.
